transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doc, I'm here because... honestly, things have just been a real mess lately. It all started when my father-in-law moved in with us. I mean, we knew he was getting older and couldn't stay in his place anymore, but the reality of him being in our house 24/7 is just... it's a lot. And ever since he got settled in the spare room, I've just been so on edge. I catch myself snapping at my wife over the most ridiculous little things around the house—like, yesterday I practically yelled at her just because she left a coffee cup on the counter, which isn't like me at all. We usually get along fine, but now I'm just so irritable. 

And it's not just that. I've been putting off all sorts of things. I used to be the guy who stayed on top of the bills, the paperwork, the little odd jobs around the house. Now, the mail just piles up on the kitchen table, and I can't even bring myself to look at it. The lawn needs mowing, the gutter is leaking, and I just... I don't care. Or I do care, but I just can't make myself do it. 

I thought maybe I just needed a break, you know? So I tried spending some time out in my workshop, tinkering with some old tools, trying to clear my head. But even out there, my mind is just racing. I can't get it to quiet down. Same thing when I tried to go fishing last weekend down at the lake. Usually, that's my peaceful place, just me and the water. But I sat there for three hours and all I could think about was the house, my father-in-law, my wife, the bills... it's like I can't escape it. I just can't seem to cope with everything right now, and my wife finally said I needed to come talk to someone before I drive us both crazy.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time since your father-in-law moved in?

Sad? Empty? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, it's not like I'm sitting around crying or feeling like life is meaningless, you know? It's really just this constant buzzing in my head, this tension. Like, the other day, I was looking out the window at the neighbor's dog running around, and normally I'd just think, 'Oh, that's nice,' but instead I was just thinking about how that dog probably doesn't have a care in the world, while I've got a house full of people and a stack of bills I can't even look at. But it's not sadness, exactly. It's more like I'm just wound up so tight that if one more thing happens—like if my father-in-law asks me how to use the TV remote one more time, which he does at least three times a day because he just can't seem to grasp the concept of the 'input' button—I'm just going to snap. So, no, not empty. If anything, I'm too full. Full of frustration, full of stress. It's just all this pressure, you know? Not sadness. Just... pressure.
Do you often find yourself worrying about the future or things that might happen?

Well, worry... I mean, I guess everybody worries a little bit, right? But it's not like I'm sitting around making lists of all the terrible things that could happen ten years from now. I'm not lying awake thinking about the economy collapsing or, you know, what if the roof caves in next winter. It's more just... the right now. The day-to-day stuff. 

Like, I'm not worried about some big imaginary future disaster. I'm just trying to figure out how I'm going to get through tomorrow with the house feeling this crowded. I mean, my father-in-law is a good guy, but he's got his routines, and they clash with ours, and I just keep thinking about how this is our life now. Is he going to need more help? Am I going to have to start driving him to every single doctor's appointment? What if he falls? But that's not really worrying about the future in that big, vague way, is it? It's just the reality of the situation staring me in the face. 

It's like, I don't have the energy to worry about what *might* happen because I'm too busy dealing with what *is* happening. The bills on the table, the tension with my wife, the constant noise in the house... it's all right there in front of me. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm a worrier about the future. I'm just overwhelmed by the present. It's just too much right now, you know? Just... right now.
Do you feel anxious most of the time?

Anxious? Um... I don't know if anxious is the right word. I mean, maybe? But it's not like my heart is pounding out of my chest or I'm having panic attacks or anything like that. It's more like... well, like I said before, it's that tension. That constant buzzing. I guess some people might call that anxiety, but to me, it just feels like I can't relax. 

Like, take the other night. My wife and I were trying to watch a movie—just trying to have a normal evening, you know? We used to do that every Friday, get a pizza, watch whatever's new on streaming. But now, my father-in-law is in the recliner right next to the couch, and he's got the volume turned up so loud because his hearing aids are always acting up, or he forgets to put them in, or whatever. And I'm sitting there, trying to focus on the movie, but all I can hear is the TV blaring and him asking every five minutes who that character is or what they just said. And I'm just sitting there, gripping the armrest, feeling my jaw clench up tighter and tighter. I'm not scared, I'm not having a panic attack, I'm just... wound up. 

So if that's what you mean by anxious, then yeah, maybe I am. But it's not this general feeling of fear. It's just that I'm constantly on high alert, waiting for the next interruption, the next thing I have to deal with, the next little annoyance that's going to push me over the edge. It's exhausting, really. I just want to sit in my own living room and watch a movie without feeling like I'm ready to explode. So, I don't know if that's anxiety or just being completely overwhelmed by everything, but it's definitely how I feel pretty much all the time now.
Have you been avoiding certain activities or situations because of the stress or tension you're feeling?

Avoiding things? Well... I mean, I guess you could say that, but it's not like I'm hiding under the covers or refusing to leave the house. It's more like... things are just slipping through the cracks because I can't focus. Like, I do—or I used to do—these small repair jobs, right? Handyman stuff. I'm not working a regular nine-to-five right now, so it was a good way to bring in some extra cash and keep busy. But lately? I just... I can't. 

Like, there was this important contractor-license filing date that I completely missed. I knew it was coming up, I had it marked on the calendar in the kitchen, but every time I walked past it, my father-in-law was there needing something, or I was just so wound up from the noise that I’d forget what I was even looking at. And because I missed that date, I've had to turn down jobs. Or I'll tell people, "Oh, I can get to that next month," just delaying and delaying because the thought of actually going over there, dealing with their problems, fixing their sink or whatever... it's just too much on top of everything here. I'm just not keeping up the way I used to. 

And it's not just the work stuff. It's happening right here at home, too. Like I said about the movie night... my wife and I used to be a team, you know? But now, there's just this real tension between us. I'm so stressed out all the time, and I know she is too, but instead of pulling together, we're just snapping at each other. I'll forget to take the trash out, or I'll say I'm going to run to the grocery store and then I just sit in the driveway for twenty minutes because I don't want to go back inside, but I don't want to go to the store either. It’s making it so much harder to just follow through on basic family responsibilities. I’m not avoiding life on purpose, it’s just that every little thing feels like climbing a mountain right now. So yeah, I guess I am avoiding things, but not because I'm scared of them. I just don't have the bandwidth for any of it anymore.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight recently?

Weight? Um... no, not really. I mean, I haven't been stepping on the scale every morning or anything like that. I think we have a scale somewhere in the master bathroom, tucked under the vanity, but honestly, I couldn't tell you the last time I pulled it out. 

I guess my clothes still fit about the same. My jeans aren't falling off me, and I'm not having to suck in my gut to button them, so I figure I'm probably hovering right around where I usually am. It's funny you ask, though, because with everything going on—with my father-in-law moving in and the tension with my wife—you'd think my eating habits would be all over the place. Like, some people stress-eat, right? They sit on the couch with a pint of ice cream or a bag of chips. Or the opposite, they get so stressed they can't eat a single bite. 

But for me, it's just... eating is just another thing I have to do. It's a chore. Like, dinner time rolls around, and it's just another source of noise and clatter in the kitchen. My father-in-law likes to eat early, like at 5:00 PM, which throws off our whole schedule. My wife and I used to eat around 7:00, after we'd had a chance to decompress, but now it's this rushed thing. We're throwing together casseroles or picking up takeout just to get it done. And I eat it, you know? I finish what's on my plate because I know I need fuel, but I'm not really tasting it or enjoying it. It's just... sustenance. 

So, yeah, my weight hasn't changed. I'm not gaining, I'm not losing. I'm just kind of stuck in the exact same spot, physically, even though mentally I feel like I'm running a marathon every single day. It's just one more thing that hasn't changed while my whole life feels upside down.
Do you often feel tired or lacking in energy?

Tired? No, I wouldn't say I'm tired. I mean, you'd think I would be, right? With all this stress and everything going on with my wife and her dad, you'd think I'd just want to crash and sleep for a week. But it's actually the exact opposite. I don't lack energy at all. If anything, I've got this... this nervous energy that I just don't know what to do with. 

Like, I'll be in the house, and I can't just sit down. I try to sit at the kitchen island with a cup of coffee in the morning, just to have five minutes of peace before the chaos starts, before the TV goes on loud enough to rattle the windows and the hearing aid complaints start. But I can't even sit there. My leg starts bouncing, and I end up getting up and pacing around. I'll wipe down the counters even if they're already clean. I'll go out to the garage—since I'm not working those handyman jobs right now anyway, like I mentioned—and I'll just start reorganizing my toolbox. I'll take all the wrenches out, sort them by size, wipe them down, put them back, and then realize I didn't even really need to do that. I'm just doing it because I have to move. 

So physically, no, my energy is fine. I'm up, I'm moving, I'm doing things, even if those things are completely pointless. It's just that my brain is fried, you know? But my body? My body is just humming with all this tension. I actually wish I *could* feel tired in that normal, heavy way. I wish I could just sink into a chair and actually relax for once. But instead, I'm just pacing holes in the rug, constantly wired, just waiting for the next shoe to drop. So, no, definitely not lacking in physical energy. It's more like I've got way too much of the wrong kind of energy, if that makes sense.
Do you often feel restless?

Yeah, exactly. Restless. I guess that’s the perfect word for what I was just trying to explain about the nervous energy and the pacing. It’s exactly that. It’s this constant... restlessness. 

Like, I’ll try to sit down on the sofa in the evenings, right? My wife and I, before her dad moved in, we used to have this routine where we’d watch an episode of something on Netflix after dinner. Just to unwind. But now? Even if we try to do that, I can't even make it through a thirty-minute sitcom. I’ll sit there, and within five minutes, I’m shifting my weight, I’m adjusting the pillows, I’m tapping my fingers on the armrest. And it drives her crazy, which just adds to that tension I was telling you about earlier. She’ll look at me and sigh, and I know she wants me to just be still, but I physically can't. It’s like my motor is running but the car is in park. 

So I’ll end up making some excuse, like, "Oh, I need to go check the mail"—even though it’s 8:00 at night and I already got the mail at noon. Or I’ll say I need a glass of water, and then I’ll just stand in the kitchen staring at the sink. I just can't settle. The whole house feels like it's vibrating, mostly because of the sheer volume of my father-in-law's TV in the other room, but also just... inside me. I’m just constantly on edge, waiting for him to yell for something or for my wife to snap at me about something I forgot to do. 

So yeah, restless is exactly it. I’m just wandering from room to room half the day, picking things up and putting them down, going out to the garage and coming back inside, because if I stop moving, I feel like I'm going to jump out of my skin. It's exhausting, honestly, but like I said, not the kind of exhausting that actually lets you just relax and be done for the day.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there's no apparent reason to worry?

Worrying for no reason? No, definitely not. I mean, I honestly wish I had the luxury of just worrying about nothing, but everything I'm stressed about is staring me right in the face. It's not like I'm sitting around making up scenarios in my head, you know? I'm not pacing the floor wondering if the roof is going to cave in, or if the economy is going to crash, or if I left the stove on. It's nothing like that. 

Every single thing that has me wound up is entirely real and happening right now in my house. I worry about how long her dad is going to be living with us, because nobody—and I mean nobody—will actually sit down and give me a straight answer on that. Is this a six-month thing? Is this permanent? I worry about that constantly, but that's a very real reason, right? And I worry about my marriage, because my wife is so stressed out taking care of him that she snaps at me if I even breathe too loudly. We used to be a team, and now I feel like I'm just in her way, which is a horrible thing to have to worry about, but again, it's actually happening. 

So, no, I don't have that thing where you just feel anxious out of the blue. For me, it's one hundred percent tied to this house and this situation. If you took my father-in-law and put him in a nice, quiet assisted living facility tomorrow, and my wife and I could just have our home back to ourselves, I wouldn't be worrying about a single thing. I'd be perfectly fine. So, I'm definitely worried, sure, but I can point to exactly what's causing it every single time. There's a very clear, very loud reason sitting in my recliner right now, so there's no mystery to it at all.
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when they are not currently happening or are unlikely to happen?

No, no, I don't think so. I mean, like I was just saying, I'm not really one of those people who sits around imagining the worst-case scenario about things that haven't even happened. It's not like I'm laying awake at night thinking, "What if a meteor hits the house?" or "What if the car breaks down on the highway next week?" I don't really let my mind wander off into those kinds of "what ifs." 

I know some people do that, my sister actually used to do that all the time. She'd get all worked up about things that were just never going to happen, like worrying about getting audited by the IRS when she barely made enough money to even file taxes, you know? But I've never been like that. I've always been a pretty practical guy. If there's a problem right in front of me, I deal with it. Or, well, I try to deal with it, even if right now I feel like I can't really do anything right. 

But as far as worrying about things that aren't happening, or things that are a million-to-one shot? No, I don't have the brain space for that right now. Every ounce of my worrying is completely taken up by the very real, very loud reality of my father-in-law blasting the TV at volume 80 and my wife acting like I'm just another piece of furniture in the way. I don't need to invent things to worry about when the actual things are taking up all my time and energy. So, no, I wouldn't say I worry about things that are unlikely to happen. The likely things are more than enough.
Are you finding it difficult to fulfill your responsibilities at home or maintain a healthy relationship with your wife due to your current stress and tension?

Yeah... yeah, it really is. It's bleeding into absolutely everything, honestly. At home, like I was hinting at earlier, the strain has put this real, heavy tension into my marriage. We're just not connecting at all right now. And because my head is just spinning all the time with this situation, it’s made it so much harder to follow through on my normal family responsibilities. Like, I’ll start a chore, maybe sorting out the garage or fixing a leaky pipe in the guest bathroom, and I just abandon it halfway through. I just can't seem to focus and get it done, which of course just frustrates my wife even more.

But it’s actually spilling over into my work, too, which is a huge problem. I do these small repair jobs, contracting work, and I actually—this is so unlike me—I missed an important contractor-license filing date recently. I’ve known the deadline was coming for months, the renewal paperwork was literally sitting right there in the kitchen under a pile of mail, but with everything going on with her dad and the house, it just completely slipped my mind until it was too late. So now I'm having to deal with that whole mess. 

And on top of it, I’ve had to start turning down or delaying these small repair jobs because I’m just not keeping up the way I used to. A guy called me the other day about fixing some drywall and a section of his deck, a job I could normally knock out in a couple of days and be glad for the work, and I just had to tell him I couldn't get to it for weeks. I just don't have the bandwidth, you know? My mind is so consumed by the stress here at the house that I can't be reliable for anybody else. So, yeah, I feel like I'm dropping the ball everywhere right now. It’s affecting my marriage, my work, my ability to just keep the house running... just everything.
Are you feeling like you're losing control over your life and relationships due to these stressors?

Yeah, losing control... that's exactly it. That's actually the whole reason I'm here talking to you right now. Because ever since my father-in-law moved in, it's like I don't even recognize myself sometimes. I've been snapping at my wife over the most ridiculous, little house things. Stuff I never would have cared about before, like if a cabinet door is left open or if there's a coffee cup left on the counter. I just snap, and then I feel terrible, but in the moment, I just have zero patience. 

And then there's the work stuff, like I was telling you before, putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay completely on top of without even trying. I've always been the guy who handles his business, you know? But now, everything just feels like this massive mountain I can't climb. 

And the worst part, the part that really makes me feel like I'm losing my grip, is that I just can't seem to get my head quiet. I try, I really do. I'll go out into my workshop, which used to be my absolute sanctuary, just to tinker with some tools or organize some things, or I'll grab my gear and go try to fish down at the lake just to get away from the house. But even out there, with nobody around, my brain is just going a million miles an hour. I'm standing there with a fishing rod in my hand, and all I can think about is the house, and I just... I can't turn it off. It's like the stress followed me right out the door and sat in the boat with me. 

So, yeah, control is definitely gone. I just want to be able to fix a piece of drywall or catch a fish without my mind racing, but I don't even know how to get back to that point anymore. It just feels like everything is slipping through my fingers.
Are you feeling like your current situation is affecting your ability to enjoy activities or spend time with people you care about?

Well, I guess it goes back to what I was just saying about the lake and my workshop. The enjoyment is just... it's just completely sucked out of it right now. 

I mean, I've got this beautiful old aluminum fishing boat that I fixed up myself a few years back. Spent months working on the hull, replacing the seats, getting this old outboard motor running perfectly. It used to be my absolute pride and joy. I’d take it out on a Saturday morning, bring a thermos of black coffee, and just... breathe, you know? Just watch the mist coming off the water. But last weekend, I took it out, and I swear to you, I didn't even notice the sunrise. I was just sitting there, gripping the fishing rod so hard my knuckles were white, completely tense, just stewing over the fact that my father-in-law had complained about the brand of orange juice I bought the day before. Over orange juice! And I'm out there on this gorgeous lake, and I can't even appreciate it. I ended up just reeling in my line and coming back home after an hour because what's the point? I can't even focus enough to enjoy the one thing that usually keeps me sane. 

And as far as spending time with people... I don't really know. I haven't really noticed a huge change there, mostly because I don't have a massive social circle to begin with. I'm a pretty independent guy. There are a couple of guys I used to do some contracting work with, you know, maybe we'd grab a beer or a burger after finishing up a tough job, but since I'm pushing off all my jobs and missing my paperwork deadlines, I'm not really seeing them anyway. 

I don't think I'm purposely hiding from my buddies or anything like that, it's more just... I don't have the energy to put on a happy face and sit at a bar making small talk about sports or whatever. If my phone rings and it's one of them, I usually just look at the screen and let it go to voicemail. I tell myself I'll call them back when things settle down at the house, but who knows when that's going to be. Right now, the only people I'm really around are my wife and her dad, and like I said, I'm actively trying *not* to spend time with them. I'm just constantly trying to find a quiet corner of the house where I don't have to deal with the tension, but honestly, it feels like there aren't any quiet corners left.
Are you feeling like you're unable to be yourself around your family due to the current situation?

Well, I wouldn't say I'm unable to be myself. I mean, what does that really mean, anyway? I'm still me. I'm still the guy who likes things a certain way, who wants to just get his work done and have a quiet house. If anything, I'm probably being exactly myself, just... the absolute worst parts of myself right now. 

I'm definitely not walking around putting on some fake smile or pretending to be happy for my father-in-law. God knows I'm not doing that. If he complains about the thermostat being too low—which he does, constantly, he always wants it at like 78 degrees, it's an absolute sauna in the living room—I don't just smile and nod and pretend it's fine. I scowl, I grumble, I probably slam a door or two on my way out to the garage. So I'm definitely showing them exactly how I feel. I wear it all right on my sleeve. 

My wife knows exactly who I am, and she knows I'm miserable right now. I'm not hiding it from her. It's just that the "me" she's getting right now is this incredibly wound-up, short-fused guy. But it's still me, you know? I've always been a bit particular about my space. Like my tools in the shop, they have a specific spot. The kitchen counters, I like them wiped down. So when he leaves his newspaper spread out all over the island, and his coffee mug leaving a ring on the wood... the old me would have been annoyed, sure, but I would have just wiped it up, maybe sighed, and moved on. The current me just completely snaps. 

But it's not like I'm a different person or I can't be myself. I'm just the maxed-out, stressed-out version of myself. I'm not putting on an act at all. Honestly, I kind of wish I could put on an act. It would probably make things a lot smoother with my wife right now if I could just fake being okay with all this disruption and pretend I'm this easygoing guy who doesn't mind his house being taken over. But I can't do that. I just can't fake it. So, yeah, I'm being myself... it's just that myself is pretty unbearable to be around at the moment.
Are you having trouble completing tasks at work or at home due to your current stress and anxiety?

Yeah, I mean, I kind of touched on the work stuff a few minutes ago, but... honestly, it’s worse than just putting off some routine paperwork. It’s actually starting to have real consequences now. 

Like, for example, I completely missed an important filing date for my contractor license recently. Just... blew right past it. And I'm the guy who usually has that stuff filled out, stamped, and mailed three weeks early. I have a whole system for it in my filing cabinet out in the shop, color-coded folders, the whole nine yards. But this year? I didn't even realize I missed the deadline until I got a notice in the mail. So now I've got to deal with late fees and jumping through all these bureaucratic hoops with the state, which is the absolute last thing I have the patience for right now. 

And because of that, and just... well, just because I'm not keeping up the way I used to in general, I've actually had to start turning down work. Small repair jobs that I normally love doing, the kind of bread-and-butter stuff that keeps me busy. I had a guy call me last week about fixing up some drywall and hanging a couple of interior doors—easy money, really, I could do it in my sleep—and I just told him my schedule was full. It wasn't full. I just... I couldn't bring myself to commit to it. I'm delaying the jobs I already have lined up, too, just pushing people off, telling them I'm waiting on materials when I haven't even ordered them yet. 

And at home... well, the home stuff is falling apart, too. The strain of everything with her dad moving in, it’s putting this huge, heavy tension right in the middle of my marriage. My wife and I are barely having a normal conversation lately that doesn't turn into an argument about him, or about something I haven't done. Because I'm definitely making it harder on her by not following through on my family responsibilities. I mean, the gutters have been completely clogged for a month. Water just spills right over the sides every time it rains, and I just stand at the kitchen window and watch it. I know I need to get the ladder out, I know it takes maybe twenty minutes to clear the leaves out, but I just... I don't do it. The trash doesn't get taken down to the curb until she gets on my case about it. It’s like I just can’t focus or muster up the drive to actually complete a single task from start to finish anymore, whether it's for a client or for my own house.
How long have you been feeling this constant tension and restlessness?

Well, let's see... it's been... I'd say right around five months now. Yeah, about five months. It basically all started right after my father-in-law moved into the house. 

I remember the timeline pretty clearly because it was right when the weather was starting to turn. We had spent the weeks before that clearing out the spare room—which, by the way, used to be my home office where I kept all my estimating software and my files, but we had to pack all of that up and shove it out into the garage to make room for his bedroom set. He showed up with all these boxes, and I honestly thought, you know, maybe there'd be a normal adjustment period. I figured, give it a couple of weeks, we'll get used to the new routine, and things will settle down. But they never settled down. The tension... it didn't take weeks to build up. It was almost immediate. 

Within just a few days of him unpacking his stuff and permanently claiming the good recliner in the living room, I just felt this... this heavy knot form right in my chest. And it hasn't gone away since. Five whole months of just walking on eggshells in my own hallway, listening to the volume on his TV blaring the news at all hours, and feeling like I can't even sit down and relax in my own home. 

I mean, five months might not sound like a lifetime when you just say it out loud, but when you're actually living it, day by day, hour by hour, it feels like an absolute eternity. Every single morning I wake up and I tell myself, okay, maybe today I won't feel so completely wound up. Maybe today I can just drink my coffee in peace and read the paper. But then I hear his slippers shuffling down the hall, and he starts complaining about a draft or about how the milk is too close to the front of the fridge, and boom, that restlessness is right back. My jaw is instantly clenched, my shoulders are up to my ears, and I'm immediately looking for an excuse to go out to a freezing cold garage just to get away from him. So yeah, it's been about five months of this exact same feeling, day in and day out, basically ever since he crossed the threshold.
Have you experienced any significant emotional or psychological distress in response to your father-in-law moving in that you feel is disproportionate to the stressor itself?

I mean, disproportionate... yeah, I suppose that’s the right word for it. Honestly, it’s exactly why I’m here talking to you today. Because, look, I know having an in-law move in is stressful for anybody. It's a classic joke, right? You see it on sitcoms all the time. But the way I'm reacting... it feels like my whole system is just short-circuiting. 

Ever since he moved in, I’ve just been snapping at my wife over the most ridiculous, tiny little house things. I mean, the other day she just asked if I'd seen where she put the good kitchen shears, and I went on this huge, blown-out rant about how nobody respects my organization system anymore and how the whole house is falling into chaos. Over scissors! She didn't deserve that at all. It's just... the pressure is so constant, and I take it out on her. 

And then there's the work stuff, which we talked about, but it really is blowing my mind how much I'm putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay on top of without even breaking a sweat. It's like I'm watching myself sabotage my own routine and I can't stop it. 

But I think the thing that really scares me, the thing that really shows how out of proportion my reaction is, is that I just can’t seem to get my head quiet anymore. Not anywhere. It used to be that if things got heavy, I'd retreat to my workshop, you know? Just me, my tools, maybe some classic rock on the radio, and I could just breathe. Or I'd grab my gear and go try to fish down at the lake for a few hours. That was my reset button. But now? I go out to the shop, I pick up a tool, and my brain is just buzzing, spinning completely out of control about the guy in my living room, the clogged gutters, the late fees... I go fishing, and I'm just staring at the water with my jaw clenched so tight my teeth hurt. I can't find a single ounce of peace inside my own skull, not even in the places that used to guarantee it. So, yeah, I'd say it's way beyond a normal reaction to having a houseguest.
Are you finding that your current symptoms are significantly interfering with your ability to function at work or in your daily life?

Well, yeah, exactly... like I was going on about a few minutes ago, it really is. It’s absolutely interfering with everything, to the point where it's practically taking over. 

I mean, I mentioned that important contractor-license filing date that I completely blew past. That’s not just a minor slip-up for me, that’s my actual ability to legally work in this state, and now I'm stuck in this endless loop of automated phone systems and state bureaucracy trying to get the late fees sorted out, which just makes me want to throw my phone against the wall. And because I’m just... I'm just not keeping up the way I used to, I’ve had to keep turning down those small repair jobs I told you about, or I'm endlessly delaying the ones I've already promised to do.
